import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "Region": ["North America", "North America", "Europe", "Europe", "Asia", "Asia",
               "Latin America", "Latin America", "Africa", "Africa", "Oceania", "Oceania"],
    "Device_Type": ["Desktop", "Mobile", "Desktop", "Mobile", "Desktop", "Mobile",
                    "Desktop", "Mobile", "Desktop", "Mobile", "Desktop", "Mobile"],
    "Avg_Purchase_Value": [58.7, 42.9, 52.5, 39.8, 85.6, 68.2, 33.1, 28.4, 25.9, 20.1, 65.3, 52.7]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
regions = df["Region"].unique()
device_types = df["Device_Type"].unique()
bar_width = 0.35
index = range(len(regions))

colors = ["#4E79A7", "#F28E2B"]

for i, device in enumerate(device_types):
    values = [df[(df["Region"] == region) & (df["Device_Type"] == device)]["Avg_Purchase_Value"].mean()
              for region in regions]
    plt.bar([p + bar_width * i for p in index], values, bar_width, label=device, color=colors[i])

plt.title("Average E-Commerce Purchase Value by Region and Device Type (2023)", fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel("Region", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Average Purchase Value (USD)", fontsize=12)
plt.xticks([p + bar_width / 2 for p in index], regions, rotation=45, ha="right")
plt.legend(title="Device Type", bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc="upper left")
plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig("output.png")

===== summary.txt
This bar chart illustrates the average e-commerce purchase value by region and device type for the year 2023. The chart compares two device types—Desktop and Mobile—across six global regions: North America, Europe, Asia, Latin America, Africa, and Oceania. The vertical axis represents the average purchase value in U.S. dollars, ranging from 0 to 90 USD, while the horizontal axis lists the regions.

Desktop purchases are represented by blue bars, and mobile purchases are represented by orange bars. In North America, the average purchase value is approximately 58.7 USD for desktop users and 42.9 USD for mobile users. Europe follows a similar pattern, with desktop purchases averaging 52.5 USD and mobile purchases averaging 39.8 USD. Asia exhibits the highest purchase values overall, with desktop purchases reaching 85.6 USD and mobile purchases at 68.2 USD. Latin America shows lower values, with desktop purchases at 33.1 USD and mobile purchases at 28.4 USD. Africa has the lowest averages, with desktop purchases at 25.9 USD and mobile purchases at 20.1 USD. Finally, Oceania’s desktop purchases average 65.3 USD, while mobile purchases average 52.7 USD.

The chart clearly demonstrates that, across all regions, desktop users tend to have a higher average purchase value compared to mobile users. The difference between device types is most pronounced in Asia and least noticeable in Latin America and Africa. The grid lines on the y-axis assist in estimating the values, and the chart includes a legend in the upper right corner to distinguish between the two device types.
